content:
### The Mystery of the Changing Sky

Have you ever looked up and wondered why the sky changes its clothes? Sometimes it wears bright blue with fluffy white cotton balls. Other times, it wears a dark blanket covered in shiny dots! Where does the Surya (Sun) go at night? And who turns on all those little lights?
**Think About It:** If the Sun is so big and bright, why can't we see it at night? Can you guess what happens to the Sun when we go to sleep?

content.title: The Earth Plays Hide and Seek
content.description: Imagine the Sun is a bright lamp in the middle of a room, and you are holding a globe. When your side of the globe faces the lamp, it's daytime. When you turn around and face away from the lamp, it's dark—that's nighttime! The Earth is constantly spinning like a top.

content: Encourage the child to use a flashlight and a ball in a dark room to simulate how the Sun lights up the Earth. This hands-on activity builds a strong intuitive understanding of day and night.
The Sun doesn't go anywhere! It's our Earth that is spinning around. So, when our side spins away from the Sun, it gets dark, and we see the Chandra (Moon) and the Tare (Stars) in the night sky.

definition: A huge ball of hot, glowing gas that gives our planet heat and light.
A large rock in space that goes around the Earth. It shines by reflecting the Sun's light.
Giant balls of hot gas far away in space that look like tiny twinkling lights from Earth.

question: Why can't we see the Sun at night?
options: Our part of the Earth spins away from the Sun.
The Moon covers the Sun completely.

content: **Reflection:** Tonight, look out your window. What shape is the moon? Is it a full circle, a half-circle, or a tiny sliver? Explain to your parents why it looks different!
Many people think the Moon actually changes its shape, but it is always a round ball! We just see different parts of it lit up by the Sun, like shining a flashlight on a ball in a dark room.

**Connection:** Did you know that long, long ago, travelers used the stars in the night sky as a map? Before GPS and smartphones, people looked at patterns in the stars to find their way across oceans and deserts. The sky is connected to everything on Earth!

**Mastery Project:** Draw two pictures of your house. In the first picture, show what the sky looks like during the day with the Sun and clouds. In the second picture, draw the night sky with the Moon and stars. See how many stars you can count and draw!
